{{short description|Russian physicist}}{{Hatnote|Not to be confused with his brother [[Alexei L. Efros]], also a physicist, or his nephew [[Alexei A. Efros]], a computer scientist.}}

'''Alexander Lvovich Efros''' ({{langx|ru|Александр Львович Эфрос}}) is a Russian [[physicist]]. Efros is the co-discoverer of semiconducting nanocrystals known as [[Quantum dot|quantum dots]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Parry |first=Daniel |date=September 26, 2013 |title=Dr. Alexander Efros Receives the E.F. Gross Medal for Pioneering Nanocrystal Research |url=https://www.nrl.navy.mil/Media/News/Article/2562574/dr-alexander-efros-receives-the-ef-gross-medal-for-pioneering-nanocrystal-resea/ |website=U.S. Naval Research Laboratory}}</ref>

Efros graduated as a physical engineer in 1973 from the [[Leningrad Technological Institute]] and received his doctorate there in 1978. He was a scientist at the [[Ioffe Institute]] in Leningrad from 1981 to 1990, at which time he moved to the West.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

In the 1980s, [[Alexey Ekimov]], Alexei A. Onuschenko and Efros, discovered [[semiconductor]] nanocrystals while studying doped glasses. They correctly determined the [[Quantum mechanics|quantum mechanical]] origin of the size-dependent optical properties of nanocrystals.<ref name=":0" />

He was at the [[Technical University of Munich]] from 1990 to 1992, at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] as visiting scientist from 1992 to 1993. Since 1993 he has been an advisor at the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Al L. Efros {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/History/Biographies/bios/Al_L_Efros |access-date=2023-10-11 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>

In 2001, Efros became a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm |access-date=2023-10-11 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref> He received the [[R. W. Wood Prize]] in 2006 along with Ekimov and [[Louis E. Brus]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=R. W. Wood Prize {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/get_involved/awards_and_honors/awards/award_descriptions/rwwood/ |access-date=2023-10-11 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-08-30 |title=Twenty attain 2006 top honors from the OSA |url=https://www.laserfocusworld.com/test-measurement/research/article/16567206/twenty-attain-2006-top-honors-from-the-osa |access-date=2023-10-11 |website=Laser Focus World}}</ref> In the [[Alexander von Humboldt Prize]] in 2008 for his work on quantum dots.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Alexander L. Efros joins Walter Schottky Institut of TUM in Garching as Senior Humboldt Fellow News|url=https://www.nano-initiative-munich.de/en/news/news/n/alexander-l-efros-joins-walter-schottky-institut-of-tum-in-garching-as-senior-humboldt-fellow/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-10-08|website=Nanosystems Initiative Munich (NIM)}}</ref> In 2013, he received the E. F. Gross Medal of the Russian Optical society for pioneering [[nanocrystal]] research.<ref name=":0" />
